bargaining_script: ഇതിന് എത്രയാണ്? (how much?) → വളരെ വിലകൂടിയതാണ്! (too pricey!) → കുറച്ച് കുറയ്ക്കൂ (reduce a little) → കിഴിവ് തരൂ (give a discount) → ശരി, പാക്ക് ചെയ്യൂ! (done, pack it!)

counting_note: Malayalam has no classifiers — put the number straight before the noun. But the noun itself goes plural with -കൾ: ഒരു പുസ്തകം (one book), രണ്ട് പുസ്തകങ്ങൾ (two books), മൂന്ന് രൂപ (three rupees).

culture.en: Kerala's harvest festival (Aug–Sep) — flower carpets, boat races and the grand സദ്യ feast on a banana leaf.
The painted-face dance-drama — one eye movement can say a whole sentence.
The backwaters — a thousand kilometres of lagoons, houseboats and village life.
The snake-boat races of Alappuzha — a hundred oarsmen rowing as one.
The traditional medicine Kerala is famous for — oil massages included.

difficulty: Medium — a new script and long agglutinative words, but verbs never conjugate
gender_note: Malayalam has masculine, feminine and neuter pronouns (അവൻ/അവൾ/അത്) — but the verbs NEVER agree with any of them. കഴിക്കുന്നു means I/you/he/she/we/they eat, all at once. Adjectives don't change either: വലിയ വീട് (big house), വലിയ കുട്ടി (big child). Gender is the easiest chapter in this course.

name: Malayalam
negation_note: ഇല്ല (illa) melts into the verb: വരില്ല (won't come), അറിയില്ല (don't know), കഴിക്കില്ല (won't eat). Alone, ഇല്ല just means 'no'. To refuse an offer, വേണ്ട (vēṇṭa — 'don't want') is warmer: ചായ വേണ്ട (no tea for me, thanks). And അല്ല (alla) denies identity: ശരിയല്ല (that's not right).

present_note: Here is Malayalam's famous gift: the present is stem + -ഉന്നു for EVERYONE. ഞാൻ, നീ, അവൻ, അവൾ, നമ്മൾ, അവർ — all take കഴിക്കുന്നു. One form, no exceptions. The table below proves it.

quiz.explain: കഴിക്കുന്നു never marks person or gender — it suits every speaker on earth.
Same verb! അവർ കഴിക്കുന്നു — Malayalam verbs never change for person. (തിന്നുക is the rude word for human eating — don't use it on people!)
വന്നു (vannu) = came — the past still never marks gender.

quiz.a: the verb stays the same for everyone

quiz.explain: പിന്നെ കാണാം (pinne kāṇām) — literally 'we'll see later' — the warm goodbye.
സുഹൃത്ത് (suhṛttŭ) = friend — കൂട്ടുകാരൻ is the casual 'buddy'.
ഇതിന് എത്രയാണ്? = how much for this — then counter with കുറച്ച് കുറയ്ക്കൂ!
നാളെ (nāḷe) = tomorrow; ഇന്നലെ (innale) = yesterday. Don't mix them at the station!

script_note: Malayalam has the roundest letters of any Indian script — all curves, no headline bar, written left to right. It is fully phonetic: each letter is one sound, always. There are 13 vowels (അ ആ ഇ ഈ ഉ ഊ ഋ എ ഏ ഐ ഒ ഓ ഔ, plus അം/അഃ) and 34 consonants, including the famous ഴ (ḻa) — a sound between r, l and d that even other Indians practise (മഴ, maḻa, rain). Letters stack into tall conjuncts: സ + ് + ത + ് + ര + ീ = സ്ത്രീ (strī, woman). Read slowly and sound every curve.
